passage:
The old playground behind the community center had rusty swings and faded slides. The city planned to remove it.
Before the work began, residents were invited to share memories. Many people came. A father said he had learned to ride a bike there. A grandmother said she had watched her children play there every summer. Teenagers remembered sitting on the swings after school.
The city still replaced the playground because it was unsafe. But it kept one old swing seat and placed it near the entrance with a small sign.
The new playground was brighter and safer. The old swing reminded everyone that a place can change without losing its story.
